shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the header that begins Agur's collection, דִּבְרֵ֤י ... הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א (oshb:Prov.30.1, "the words of Agur ... the oracle"), and runs through a first-person meditation on the limits of human knowledge before God (30:2-4) into an affirmation that God's own word is tested and trustworthy (30:5) and a warning not to add to it, אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל דְּבָרָ֑יו (oshb:Prov.30.6, "do not add to his words"). The skeleton דִּבְרֵ֤י occurs in 19 verses book-wide (sweep: 19), of which 9 are genuine construct-state "words of X" forms (1.6, 12.6, 18.4, 18.8, 22.12, 22.17, 26.22, 30.1, 31.1); the remaining 10 are pronominal-suffixed ("my/your/his words": 1.23, 4.4, 4.20, 23.8, 29.20, 30.6) or absolute-plural ("words": 10.19, 24.26, 26.6, 29.19) forms of the same root. Of the 19, the construct form opens the verse in 5 (sweep: 5 of 19, the verse-initial subset), and pairs with an oracle-word to form an actual collection header in only 2 of those 5 (sweep: 2 of 5) -- here and again at the Lemuel header. The petuchah recorded at oshb:Prov.30.6 (single-witness) corroborates this seam before the numbered petition that begins the next unit.
